title: The Famous Equation of Statistical Thermodynamics is S=k ln W
lead: Boltzmann tied entropy to a count: the number of microstates that give the same macrostate. His formula, carved on his grave, turns that count into an entropy, here for a crystal whose molecules can point two ways.
notes: Adapted from Patrick E. Fleming (California State University, East Bay) and Jerry LaRue (Chapman University).
exercise_notes: The book sets no exercises for this section; the one exercise, on a crystal whose molecules take four orientations, was written by AI with an AI solution. Its Bloom level and concept tags were chosen by AI. Numeric answers accept a 2% tolerance.

exercises.prompt: In a crystal of 1.00 mol of a compound, each molecule can sit in any one of four equivalent orientations, independently of the others. Find the entropy that this orientational freedom contributes, in J/K. Why is $W$ not simply 4?

answer.hint: Each of the $N$ molecules chooses its orientation on its own, so the counts multiply.
answer.solution: Each of the $N = nN_A$ molecules has four choices, and the choices are independent, so the number of microstates is $W = 4^{N}$, not 4: a value of 4 would describe a single molecule. Then $\kSent = k\ln W = Nk\ln 4 = nN_Ak\ln 4 = nR\ln 4 = (1.00\ \text{mol})(8.314\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1})(1.386) = 11.53\ \text{J/K}$, twice the 5.76 J/K of the two orientations in Example 20.5.1, since $\ln 4 = 2\ln 2$.

footnotes.html: The book writes $S = nK\ln(W)$ with $W = 2$. Each of the $N = nN_A$ molecules takes one of two orientations, so $W = 2^{N}$ and $S = k\ln 2^{N} = nN_Ak\ln 2 = nR\ln 2$, which gives the 5.76 J/K printed. The $\cot$ in the next line stands for a multiplication sign.
